1.0 INTRODUCTION:

1.1 To define the policies regarding (Normal Labor and Caesarean Section) care.

2.0 SCOPE:

2.1 Hospital Management

2.2 Health Care Providers

2.3 Patients

3.0 RESPONSIBILITY:

3.1 Ayurved MD in Stri and Prasuti Tantra

3.2 On call Gynecologist

3.3 On call Pediatrician

3.4 Nursing staff

3.5 Anesthesiologist

3.6 Labor Room staff

3.7 NBCC staff

3.8 Dietitian

4.0 ABBREVIATIONS:

4.1 COP-Care of Patient

5.0 DEFINITION: Nil

6.0 REFERENCE:

6.1 NABH: Accreditation Standards for Ayurveda Hospitals 2nd Edition April 2016.

7.0 OBJECTIVE ELEMENTS

7.1. There is a documented policy and procedure for obstetric (Normal Labor and Caesarean Section) services.

7.2 Persons caring for high-risk obstetric cases are competent.

7.3 Appropriate Peri-natal monitoring is performed and documented.

7.4 The organization caring for high-risk obstetric cases has the facilities to take care of neonates of such cases.

8. 0 PROCESSES

8.1 SOP OF LABOR (caesarian section not done, cases are referred to SMHRC) Management of a Patient in the 1st stage of labor

Role of Midwife

• Conduct a physical assessment including abdominal palpation on the client/patient

• Assess the vital signs and urine analysis of the client/patient.

• Assess, monitor and record the duration, frequency and intensity of uterine contractions.

• Monitor the fetal heart rate to assess fetal well-being. Monitor the client/patient’s coping ability as labor progresses.

• Offer, in accordance with National Guidelines, HIV screening.

• Obtain fetal heart rate pattern of all high risk clients, inform the obstetrician on call and attach to client’s records.

• Conduct vaginal examinations.

• Report immediately any abnormal signs, symptoms and findings to the Obstetrician

• Communicate the findings of her assessment to the client and/ or immediate family as Appropriate

• Provide supportive care for the client/patient in terms of ambulation, nutrition, personal hygiene, breathing/relaxation techniques and general progress of labor.

• Develop an individualized plan of care in collaboration with the client/patient.

• Prepare clients for delivery when labor is established and progressive.

• Employ pain management techniques in accordance with established pain management protocols and guidelines

• Ensure that the client's bowel and bladder are emptied.

• Ensure that emergency equipment, medication and consumables are available and functional in preparation for delivery of the newborn.

Role of Obstetrician

• Collaborate and communicate with staff at the support units/departments for timely Intervention in case of an emergency

• Communicate with the Neonatologist/Pediatrician for timely intervention in case of an emergency.

• Advice, support and assist the client during labor.

• Ensure that he/she is readily available to manage any complication/s that may arise during labor and/or delivery.

Management of the client in 2nd stage of labor

PROCEDURE

• Ensure that the birthing area is prepared for the delivery of the newborn

• Ensure that the infant incubator or cot is prepared and positioned for receiving the Newborn.

• Advice and support the client on the position to be adopted for delivery.

• Ensure that the required Protective Personal Equipment is worn in preparation for delivery.

• Ensure that adequate privacy is provided during the birthing process.

• Maintain communication with the client and guide her through the birthing process

• Announce to the staff the gender and time of birth of the newborn upon delivery.

• Allow the mother to cuddle the newborn and confirm the gender immediately after birth.

• Perform nasal and oral suctioning of the newborn following delivery as required

• Ensure that a Neonatologist/Pediatrician is present at all deliveries where the babies are at risk.

• Administer intramuscular oxytocin to the client as per medication protocol.

• Record the time and date of birth, gender of newborn and maternal name on the I.D. bracelet.

• Conduct physical assessment on the newborn and assign an APGAR score.

• Administer Vitamin K to the newborn as per medication protocol.

• Perform cord care; the newborn is then clothed and wrapped to maintain body heat.

• Transport the newborn to the mother in a cot and initiate breastfeeding unless otherwise indicated.

Pain Management in Labor

• Remind the client/patient of the techniques taught to her during her childbirth education.

• Offer alternative techniques in labor which enhances comfort e.g. squatting, laboring in water.

• Offer oxygen inhalation as per medication protocol

• Offer medication (Tramadol/drotin) as per medication protocol.

• Offer regional analgesic techniques as clinically indicated.

• Ensure appropriate documentation in the client/patient’s record.

Management of the client in 3rd stage of labor

• Deliver the placenta and membranes.

• Assess the perineum, vaginal floor and cervix for lacerations and then apply a sterile Sanitary pad

• Assess the blood loss and uterine tone

• Ensure that the client is made comfortable in bed following delivery.

• Ensure that the post-delivery vital signs are monitored and recorded.

• Examine the placenta and membranes for completeness, record findings and report concerns.

• Obtain cord blood for laboratory analysis. (E.g. RH negative & O positive mothers)

• Measure the blood loss.

• Allow the client to rest for a minimum of 1hr following delivery before transfer to the Post-natal ward unless otherwise indicated.

• Ensure that all care is documented in the client’s health record.

Management of Complications Of The Third Stage Of Labor

PROLONGED THIRD STAGE OF LABOR

• Attempt to deliver the placenta by continuous cord traction.

• Inform the Obstetrician on duty if continuous cord traction fails.

• Ensure that a urinary catheter is inserted and attached to a closed drainage system

• Obtain blood for Group & Cross Match.

• Ensure an intravenous access and infusion is established.

• Assess and record the vital signs of the client.

• Alert the Operating theatre staff and Anesthetist.

• Ensure the client is informed of and understands the plan of care.

• Administer prophylactic antibiotics as prescribed.

• Assess client and confirm the plan of care

• Prepare a client for manual removal of placenta.

• Inform client of the plan of care for removal of the placenta and obtain informed Consent

• Inform immediate relatives/significant others of a plan of care.

• Prescribe prophylactic antibiotics

Management of the client in 4th stage of labor

PROCEDURE:

• Ensure that the client’s uterus is well contracted and assess the volume and nature of lochia.

• Assess the coping ability of the client and provide the required support and comfort.

• Prepare the client for perineal repair which shall be done within 1 hr following delivery.

• Inform the Obstetrician and Pediatrician of any abnormalities.

• Ensure that the client’s vital signs are monitored and recorded.

• Support the mother with bonding and breastfeeding during this period unless contraindicated.

• Offer a light meal or refreshment as desired unless contraindicated.

• Monitor and support the mother in the care of her newborn until transfer to the postnatal ward.

• Make assessments of the client’s lochia, fundal height and bladder function during the post-partum period.

• Document all findings in the client’s health record.

• Prepare the client for transfer to the postnatal ward. Follow established infection prevention and control guidelines.

Breech Presentation in labor

• Each Obstetric/Midwifery: Unit will develop individual Guidelines for Management of the breech delivery.

PROCEDURE

• Conduct an abdominal examination and document findings in the client’s health record.

• Perform a sterile vaginal examination to

(a) assess cervical dilation

(b) confirm the presenting part and

(c) exclude cord presentation/ prolapse.

• Inform the on-call Obstetrician of the findings of the abdominal and vaginal examination.

• Inform the Operating theatre, Anesthetist and Neonatologist/Pediatrician of the pending delivery.

• Discuss the plan of care with the client to facilitate her active participation.

• Employ pain management in accordance with written protocols and procedures.

• Conduct continuous electronic fetal monitoring during the labor.

• Collaborate with the Obstetrician to determine the appropriate mode of delivery after confirming the presentation.

• Provide support and guidance to the client throughout the delivery process.

• In the absence of the obstetrician, the midwife shall perform the breech delivery.

• Ensure that the Obstetrician and Neonatologist/Pediatrician are present at a breech delivery.

• Follow established infection prevention and control guidelines

• Respond to the call from the Midwife in a timely manner

• Perform the breech delivery if requested.

DYSTOCIA

PROCEDURE

• Recognize the problem and call for assistance.

• Call Registrar/Consultant, anesthetist and pediatrician.

• Note the time of delivery of the head.

• Explain the procedure to the client to gain her cooperation.

• Avoid fundal pressure and extensive traction on the fetal neck.

• Perform an episiotomy if possible.

• Conduct the Mc Roberts maneuver.

• Apply suprapubic pressure over the fetal anterior shoulder.

• Attempt to deliver the posterior shoulder

• Ensure the pediatrician is present for the delivery as well as ensuring that resuscitative equipment is present and functional.

• Follow established infection prevention and control guidelines according to the IPC manual.

Post delivery procedures:

• Note time of delivery of baby

• Time of call for assistance

• Baby’s condition

• Names of staff present

• Complete incident form

• Affix signature

• Explain the procedure to the client including the inherent risks and obtain informed consent.

• Attempt different maneuvers to deliver the baby and if all else fails then Zavannelli maneuver should be considered.

• Alert Operating theatre staff and anesthetist, client/patient to be transferred to the OT if all attempts fail.

• Complete the Shoulder Dystocia form.

• Follow established infection prevention and control guidelines according to the IPC manual.

FORCEPS DELIVERY

PROCEDURE

• Determine the indication for a forceps delivery.

• Communicate with the client/patient on the need for a forceps delivery.

• Ensure that the pediatrician is present during the delivery.

• Explain the procedure to the client/patient including the inherent risks and obtain informed consent.

• Apply the appropriate technique in conducting the delivery in keeping with established guidelines.

• Examine for any traumatic lacerations to the maternal genital tract and rectum/anal sphincter and perform timely repair.

• Document all information related to the procedure.

• Follow established infection prevention and control guidelines according to the MoH Infection, Prevention and Control Manual.

VENTOUSE EXTRACTION

• Inform the Neonatologist/Pediatrician and alert the Operating Theatre staff.

• Ensure that the period of gestation is greater than 34 weeks.

• Choose the appropriate size cup that will fit the baby’s head.

• Ensure that no cervix or the vaginal wall is trapped beneath the rim of the cup.

• Establish gentle suction while the client continues to push during contractions.

• Perform episiotomy during the crowning of the head.

• Release suction and remove the cup once the head is delivered and complete delivery as normal.

• Follow established infection prevention and control guidelines according to the IPC manual.

• Prepare the client/patient and the environment of care for the conduct of the delivery.

• Provide support and counseling for the client and family throughout the delivery.

• Assist the Obstetrician in the conduct of the delivery.

• Assist the Neonatologist/Pediatrician in the resuscitation of the newborn and ensure that the APGAR score is recorded.

• Ensure that all care is documented accurately and in a timely manner.

• Ensure that assessment of vital signs are made and recorded in the client’s Health Record.

• Monitor and record

✓ The client’s vital signs

✓ Lochia

✓ Coping patterns

• Provide emotional support for the mother and immediate family members.

• Follow established Infection, Prevention and Control Guidelines according to the MoHInfection, Prevention and Control Manual.

• Ensure that the Neonatologist/Pediatrician is present at all instrumental deliveries

• Ensure that all available resuscitative equipment and supplies are functional.
